articles.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to large prisoner swap; no breakthrough on ending the war
articles.summary:
Two days of US-mediated talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi ended on Wednesday with agreement on a large exchange of prisoners of war. Russia's chief negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, said both sides had agreed to the swap. Ukraine's delegation was led by Rustem Umerov.

No ceasefire was agreed. US envoy Jared Kushner said territorial issues would be the hardest to settle but that progress was made on a post-war security framework. He said he and Steve Witkoff would travel to Moscow to brief Vladimir Putin and then meet Volodymyr Zelensky in Dublin.
keyFacts: Final prisoner numbers had not been set when the talks ended
Russian state agency TASS said the exchange should happen within two to three weeks
It was the first meeting between the two delegations in about nine months

articles.title: Qantas to cut 850 corporate jobs in outsourcing deal with Accenture
articles.summary:
Qantas told staff on Tuesday it will cut 850 positions after signing an outsourcing deal with consultancy Accenture. The first phase covers finance, procurement, human resources and marketing, with the Sydney headquarters most affected. AAP reports most of Accenture's work for Qantas will be done in India, with some roles staying in Australia.

Chief executive Vanessa Hudson linked the move to modernising technology and the impact of AI. The Australian Services Union criticised the cuts as sending skills offshore. Transport Minister Catherine King called the decision extremely disappointing.
keyFacts: 850 positions; some reports put the total near 1,000
Qantas reported a $1.3 billion net profit for 2025/26 in August
Qantas says it will consult affected staff and redeploy where possible

articles.title: US inflation comes in higher than forecast, raising odds of a Fed rate rise
articles.summary:
US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported, above the 0.3% economists expected. Core prices, which exclude food and energy, rose 0.3% against a forecast of 0.2%. The bureau could not publish annual figures because it collected no data in October 2025, during the government shutdown.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said before the release that a half-point rate rise should be considered in December if core inflation came in around 0.3%. US shares and Treasuries fell after the data, and the ASX was expected to open lower.
keyFacts: Headline CPI +0.4% for the month; core +0.3%
September's headline rise was 0.6%
Markets raised the odds of a December rate hike

articles.title: US House shelves Hegseth impeachment; Jordan to lead Republicans in new Congress
articles.summary:
The US House voted 211–204 to refer Republican Thomas Massie's impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, which effectively ends it for now. The articles accuse Hegseth of conducting hostilities against Iran without congressional authorisation. Massie was the only Republican to vote against the referral. Eleven Democrats and seven Republicans did not vote.

Separately, House Republicans elected Jim Jordan over Steve Scalise, 106–73 according to CBS News sources, to lead them when they become the minority in January.
keyFacts: Vote was on a motion to refer, not on impeachment itself
11 Democrats were absent; the margin was 7
Senate Republicans re-elected John Thune as leader

articles.title: US charges three men over alleged Iran-backed plots in Europe and the US
articles.summary:
Federal prosecutors in New York unsealed an indictment charging three men over what they describe as a campaign of nearly 20 attacks targeting Jewish communities in Europe and the US, plus a plot against RAF Fairford, a British base used by US forces. Prosecutors allege the men acted for Iran's Revolutionary Guard and the Iraqi militia Kata'ib Hezbollah. Only one of the three, Mohammad Baqer al-Saadi, is in custody.

Iran has denied involvement in the Fairford incident. Separately, UK police arrested a US Army soldier on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence.
keyFacts: Three men charged; only al-Saadi is in custody
Al-Saadi pleaded not guilty in June to earlier charges
The UK soldier arrest is a separate case

articles.title: Israel's new parliament sworn in with no bloc holding a majority
articles.summary:
Israel's 26th Knesset was sworn in on Tuesday. Neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposing bloc holds the 61 seats needed to govern. President Isaac Herzog gave opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the first mandate to form a government on 8 November, giving him 28 days.

Netanyahu called on opposition parties to join a unity government under his leadership. Eisenkot's bloc sought a vote to replace Speaker Amir Ohana of Likud at the opening session. Ohana said such a vote required 61 signatures.
keyFacts: Likud is the largest party with 27 seats
Eisenkot has 28 days to form a coalition
ABC reported heckling during Netanyahu's speech

articles.title: COP31: rooftop solar declaration unveiled; Australia was first to sign
articles.summary:
The Global Solar Council unveiled a Global Rooftop Solar Declaration at the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Signatory governments commit to helping double the number of homes with rooftop solar, from about 150 million to 300 million, by 2030. The declaration is voluntary and non-binding.

Australia became the first country to endorse it in October, when Energy Minister Chris Bowen, who is COP31's president of negotiations, signed at a Pacific pre-COP meeting in Fiji. ABC reports negotiators are split over a separate electrification target.
keyFacts: COP31 runs 9–20 November in Antalya
Target: 300 million solar homes by 2030
More than a third of Australian homes have rooftop solar

articles.title: Nvidia board investigates reports CEO was target of foreign intelligence effort
articles.summary:
Nvidia's board said on 8 November it was opening an independent investigation into reports that chief executive Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors with outside counsel will run it. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

The New York Times reported in October that US officials concluded Megaspeed executive Alice Huang was passing information to Beijing. China denies this. Jensen Huang told staff he had been unfaithful to his wife. Nvidia shares fell more than 4% on Monday.
keyFacts: Investigation is internal; no charges reported
Huang remains CEO and says he will cooperate
Shares closed at US$178.67 on 9 November

articles.title: RBA economist says AI investment is adding to demand before productivity gains show
articles.summary:
Reserve Bank chief economist Sarah Hunter said on Monday that AI is already reshaping the Australian economy through business investment and demand. AAP reports there is so far limited evidence that AI is lifting productivity. RBA staff estimate data centre investment has grown roughly tenfold in three years and project a further $115 billion by the end of 2028.

RBA research found households' exposure to AI-related shares, mostly through super, rose from about 2% of financial wealth in 2022 to 5.3% in June 2026. Staff estimate a 30% fall in those shares would cut household wealth by 1.6%.
keyFacts: Speech delivered 9 November in Sydney
AI-related memory chip prices rose more than 200% in a year, per RBA research
The $115 billion projection depends on power, water and construction capacity

articles.title: Israeli strikes kill at least 10 in Gaza over two days, health officials say
articles.summary:
Israeli forces killed at least seven Palestinians in Gaza on Tuesday, including a father and his 13-year-old son, local health officials told Reuters. Medics said the two were killed when an airstrike hit the roof of a displacement shelter in Gaza City's Zeitoun neighbourhood. On Wednesday, strikes killed three more people, including two brothers at a tent for displaced people.

The Israeli military said it struck militants in the areas, without giving details. Gaza's Health Ministry says more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began in October 2025.
keyFacts: At least 7 killed Tuesday and 3 Wednesday, per local health officials
The Israeli military says it targeted militants
The ceasefire took effect in October 2025

articles.title: House Republicans' Epstein report says federal government failed survivors
articles.summary:
Republicans on the US House Oversight Committee released a report on Tuesday concluding their 15-month investigation into Jeffrey Epstein. It found the federal government mishandled criminal investigations into Epstein over decades and failed survivors. It drew on 19 witness interviews and depositions and on documents subpoenaed from the Justice Department, Epstein's estate and two banks.

The report said the facts uncovered do not suggest President Trump was implicated in Epstein's crimes. It accused committee Democrats of trying to implicate him. It identified two former federal prosecutors whose role in the original case raised concerns, according to Fox News.
keyFacts: Report runs to about 136 pages
Released by the Republican majority under chair James Comer
Next steps are left to the Justice Department

leftOut.title: Iran repeats it will not send enriched uranium abroad; US keeps focus on sanctions
leftOut.summary:
Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, said again this week that none of Iran's enriched nuclear material will leave the country. He first made the statement publicly on 20 October during a visit by Pakistan's army chief, Asim Munir.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said economic pressure, including a naval blockade, has reduced the need for major combat. Axios first reported in August that Rubio told allies the US was shifting from strikes to sanctions, without ruling out force if Iran attacks first.
keyFacts: Iran says its enriched material is for use only inside the country
US strategy: naval blockade plus Treasury sanctions
Both positions have been stated before

leftOut.title: Spain's main unions hold first 24-hour general strike since 2012 over housing and wages
leftOut.summary:
Spain's two largest union federations, UGT and CCOO, called a 24-hour general strike for Wednesday 11 November over housing costs and wages. Tenants' unions and other groups joined the call. It is the first general strike backed by the major unions since 2012.

The strike falls just over two weeks before a snap general election on 29 November. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called the election after Congress rejected two government housing decrees. The official campaign starts on 13 November.
keyFacts: Strike called for 00:00–24:00 on 11 November
General election on 29 November
Unions registered the strike with the Labour Ministry on 19 October

leftOut.title: Digital duty of care bill awaits Senate committee report due 20 November
leftOut.summary:
The Online Safety Amendment (Digital Duty of Care) Bill 2026 passed the House of Representatives on 28 October and is now before the Senate. It would place a legal duty on online services, including social media, search engines and generative AI services, to take reasonable steps to keep Australians safe, with extra protections for under-18s.

Companies that breach the duty could face penalties of up to about $109 million. The government has backed changes aimed at AI chatbots that simulate emotional intimacy with children. The Greens want stronger penalties.
keyFacts: Introduced by Communications Minister Anika Wells
Passed the House on 28 October
Senate committee report due 20 November

leftOut.title: Pope Leo draws an estimated 2.5 million to Buenos Aires Mass on first papal visit to Argentina since 1987
leftOut.summary:
Pope Leo XIV celebrated an open-air Mass in Buenos Aires on 9 November that officials estimated drew 2.5 million people, the largest gathering of his papacy. The same day he met victims of clergy abuse. He celebrated Mass in Córdoba on 10 November and visited Luján on 11 November.

It is the first papal visit to Argentina since 1987. The 12-day trip also covers Uruguay and Peru and ends on 17 November.
keyFacts: Argentina leg ran 8–11 November
The Pope met President Javier Milei during the visit
Next stop: Peru

leftOut.title: Khawaja memoir claims whole Australian team knew about 2018 ball-tampering plan
leftOut.summary:
Former Test opener Usman Khawaja claims in his memoir Sabr that the whole Australian team knew of the 2018 ball-tampering plan in Cape Town. He also says similar tactics were discussed during the previous Test in Port Elizabeth. That contradicts the Cricket Australia investigation, which found only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft knew.

Khawaja told captain Pat Cummins and Cricket Australia chief Todd Greenberg about the chapter before the team's South Africa tour. AAP reported he has since cut back some book-tour appearances.
keyFacts: Book published by Penguin Australia in November
The 2018 investigation named only three players
Other players' accounts differ from Khawaja's

leftOut.title: David Walliams faces further allegations; he denies wrongdoing
leftOut.summary:
Comedian and children's author David Walliams faced further allegations this week of inappropriate behaviour towards young women, in reporting by The Guardian and ITV. HarperCollins dropped him in December 2025 after an internal investigation, and in September 2026 it stopped publishing his back catalogue.

Walliams strongly denies behaving inappropriately. His spokesperson has said he was never told of the allegations or given a chance to respond to the publisher's investigation.
keyFacts: HarperCollins dropped him in December 2025
His back catalogue was dropped in September 2026
He denies all allegations

leftOut.title: Meghan's father Thomas Markle Sr. charged with possessing child abuse material
leftOut.summary:
Thomas Markle Sr., 82, the estranged father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, was arrested by the FBI in Florida on 6 November. He is charged with one count of possession of child sexual abuse material, according to the US Attorney's Office. The material was allegedly found in two storage units he rented in the Los Angeles area.

He has not entered a plea, and the allegations have not been tested in court. Meghan described the allegations as deeply disturbing.
keyFacts: Arrested 6 November near Tampa
Charged on a federal criminal complaint
Maximum penalty if convicted: 20 years

leftOut.title: Harry and Meghan speak at European Parliament event on social media harms to children
leftOut.summary:
Prince Harry and Meghan attended an event at the European Parliament in Brussels on 10 November. It opened a memorial installation showing images of 50 children who died after harm they suffered on social media. Parliament President Roberta Metsola was also due to speak.

It was the couple's first public appearance since the allegations against Meghan's father emerged. Harry has campaigned on the risks of social media and AI chatbots for young people.
keyFacts: Event at the European Parliament, Brussels
The installation is called the Lost Screen Memorial
Harry spoke on AI chatbots and children in September
